chapter: Reel 1: childhood, first songs, Fats Waller
title: His favorite tune, 'Traveling All Alone'
summary: He names 'Traveling All Alone' as his favorite; Rasch says 'One Day' makes her cry.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: Listening to classical music, then and now

blocks.x: Right. All right, now what do you think -- what, of your favorite song, favorite song - composition, music, that you ever wrote ... what is it? Do you have a favorite?

That's something that I don't know whether anyone really actually knows -- the favorite that they love the most. They'll give you one; they'll say, "Well, I like this one the best" and then a month later, they'd say, "Gee whiz, I shouldn't have said that, I should've said this".
But I don't know of any other tune than a tune called "Traveling All Alone".
I heard you play that at Harmony Hall. That's when I fell in love with you.
Well, that is my favorite tune.
Oh, you did tell me one.
I want to know why. When you play "One Day" for me, I always cry.
Oh? I don't know, I'll have to play that for you for awhile, I haven't played that for you for a long time.
And I'd like to play it because that is a beautiful thing if ever there was one --and you recognize beauty, it's the beauty in it that comes, that saturates itself with you.

That's all; it just gets under your skin, the beauty of that. To me, I can sit and just play that thing -- I love it, and we love it. I won't say I love it, we love it -- we -- you and I, we both love that tune.
